claim: Congenital cataract is one of the leading causes of blindness in children.
source: Congenital cataract, an ocular disease predominantly occurring within the first decade of life, is one of the leading causes of blindness in children.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by citation to literature.

claim: Congenital cataract accounts for 5–20% blindness in children worldwide.
source: It is a common ocular abnormality that causes visual impairment and blindness during infancy (Khokhar et al., 2017), accounting for 5–20% blindness in children worldwide (Sheeladevi et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sheeladevi et al., 2016.

claim: A potential pathological variant (p.G1943E) in PIKFYVE was identified through whole-exome sequencing of a Chinese family with congenital cataract.
source: Through whole-exome sequencing of a Chinese family with congenital cataract, we identified a potential pathological variant (p.G1943E) in PIKFYVE, which is located in the PIP kinase domain of the PIKFYVE protein.
evidence: The study performed WES and identified the variant.

claim: The p.G1943E variant is located in the PIP kinase domain of the PIKFYVE protein.
source: Through whole-exome sequencing of a Chinese family with congenital cataract, we identified a potential pathological variant (p.G1943E) in PIKFYVE, which is located in the PIP kinase domain of the PIKFYVE protein.
evidence: The location of the variant is determined by sequence analysis.

claim: Heterozygous/homozygous disruption of PIKFYVE kinase domain in zebrafish mimicked the cataract defect in human patients.
source: We demonstrated that heterozygous/homozygous disruption of PIKFYVE kinase domain, instead of overexpression of PIKFYVEG1943E in zebrafish mimicked the cataract defect in human patients, suggesting that haploinsufficiency, rather than dominant-negative inhibition of PIKFYVE activity caused the disease.
evidence: Zebrafish experiments showed cataract phenotype upon disruption of PIKFYVE.

claim: Overexpression of PIKFYVEG1943E in zebrafish did not mimic the cataract defect in human patients.
source: We demonstrated that heterozygous/homozygous disruption of PIKFYVE kinase domain, instead of overexpression of PIKFYVEG1943E in zebrafish mimicked the cataract defect in human patients, suggesting that haploinsufficiency, rather than dominant-negative inhibition of PIKFYVE activity caused the disease.
evidence: Zebrafish overexpression experiments did not produce cataract phenotype.

claim: Haploinsufficiency, rather than dominant-negative inhibition of PIKFYVE activity caused the disease.
source: We demonstrated that heterozygous/homozygous disruption of PIKFYVE kinase domain, instead of overexpression of PIKFYVEG1943E in zebrafish mimicked the cataract defect in human patients, suggesting that haploinsufficiency, rather than dominant-negative inhibition of PIKFYVE activity caused the disease.
evidence: Inferred from the differential effects of disruption versus overexpression in zebrafish.

claim: Loss of Pikfyve caused aberrant vacuolation in lens cells of pikfyve zebrafish mutants.
source: Phenotypical analysis of pikfyve zebrafish mutants revealed that loss of Pikfyve caused aberrant vacuolation (accumulation of Rab7+Lc3+ amphisomes) in lens cells, which was significantly alleviated by treatment with the V-ATPase inhibitor bafilomycin A1 (Baf-A1).
evidence: Microscopy analysis of zebrafish mutants showed vacuolation.

claim: The aberrant vacuolation in pikfyve zebrafish mutants represents accumulation of Rab7+Lc3+ amphisomes.
source: Phenotypical analysis of pikfyve zebrafish mutants revealed that loss of Pikfyve caused aberrant vacuolation (accumulation of Rab7+Lc3+ amphisomes) in lens cells, which was significantly alleviated by treatment with the V-ATPase inhibitor bafilomycin A1 (Baf-A1).
evidence: Marker analysis showed co-localization with Rab7 and Lc3.

claim: Treatment with bafilomycin A1 (Baf-A1) significantly alleviated the aberrant vacuolation in pikfyve zebrafish mutants.
source: Phenotypical analysis of pikfyve zebrafish mutants revealed that loss of Pikfyve caused aberrant vacuolation (accumulation of Rab7+Lc3+ amphisomes) in lens cells, which was significantly alleviated by treatment with the V-ATPase inhibitor bafilomycin A1 (Baf-A1).
evidence: Drug treatment experiments showed reduction in vacuole numbers.

claim: PIKFYVE is a novel causative gene for congenital cataract.
source: Collectively, we identified PIKFYVE as a novel causative gene for congenital cataract and pinpointed the potential application of Baf-A1 for the treatment of congenital cataract caused by PIKFYVE deficiency.
evidence: Based on genetic and functional studies in this manuscript.

claim: Baf-A1 has potential application for the treatment of congenital cataract caused by PIKFYVE deficiency.
source: Collectively, we identified PIKFYVE as a novel causative gene for congenital cataract and pinpointed the potential application of Baf-A1 for the treatment of congenital cataract caused by PIKFYVE deficiency.
evidence: Based on the rescue effect observed in zebrafish experiments.

claim: Autosomal dominant congenital cataract is the most common mode of inheritance.
source: A variety of factors, including gene variants that affect lens metabolism. are closely associated with cataract (Li et al., 2020), and autosomal dominant congenital cataract is the most common mode of inheritance (Berry et al., 2020a).
evidence: Supported by citation to Berry et al., 2020a.

claim: The occurrence of congenital cataract has been linked with genetic variants in at least 50 genes involved in lens structure and development.
source: To date, the occurrence of congenital cataract has been linked with genetic variants in at least 50 genes involved in lens structure and development (Berry et al., 2020b; Shiels and Hejtmancik, 2017), including crystallin genes (CRYAA, CRYAB, CRYBB1, CRYBB2, CRYBB3, CRYBA1/A3, CRYBA2, CRYBA4, CRYGC, CRYGD, and CRYGS) (Bhat, 2003; Zhuang et al., 2019), membrane protein genes (GJA3, GJA8, MIP, and LIM2) (Berry et al., 2000; Beyer et al., 2013; Pei et al., 2020), growth and transcription factor genes (PITX3, MAF, and HSF4) (Anand et al., 2018), beaded filament structural protein genes (BFSP1 and BFSP2) (Song et al., 2009), and other genes (CHMP4B and EPHA2) (Dave et al., 2016; Shiels et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to literature.

claim: The human PIKFYVE gene encodes a large protein consisting of 2098 amino acids.
source: The human PIKFYVE gene encodes a large protein consisting of 2098 amino acids, which contains six evolutionarily conserved domains (Kawasaki et al., 2012), including zinc finger phosphoinositide kinase (FYVE) domain, plextrin homology domain, β-sheet winged helix DNA/RNA-binding motif, cytosolic chaperone CCTγ apical domain-like motif, spectrin repeats (SPEC), and C-terminal fragment PIPK domain (Li et al., 2005; Shisheva, 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kawasaki et al., 2012; Li et al., 2005; Shisheva, 2008.

claim: PIKFYVE contains six evolutionarily conserved domains.
source: The human PIKFYVE gene encodes a large protein consisting of 2098 amino acids, which contains six evolutionarily conserved domains (Kawasaki et al., 2012), including zinc finger phosphoinositide kinase (FYVE) domain, plextrin homology domain, β-sheet winged helix DNA/RNA-binding motif, cytosolic chaperone CCTγ apical domain-like motif, spectrin repeats (SPEC), and C-terminal fragment PIPK domain (Li et al., 2005; Shisheva, 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kawasaki et al., 2012; Li et al., 2005; Shisheva, 2008.

claim: The N-terminal FYVE domain of PIKFYVE can bind to PtdIns3P on the membrane.
source: The N-terminal FYVE domain can bind to PtdIns3P on the membrane, while the C-terminal is the kinase domain which has the catalytic function for the production of PtdIns(3,5)P2 (Shisheva et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by citation to Shisheva et al., 1999.

claim: The C-terminal kinase domain of PIKFYVE has the catalytic function for the production of PtdIns(3,5)P2.
source: The N-terminal FYVE domain can bind to PtdIns3P on the membrane, while the C-terminal is the kinase domain which has the catalytic function for the production of PtdIns(3,5)P2 (Shisheva et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by citation to Shisheva et al., 1999.

claim: The in-vivo function of PIKFYVE in the development of lens and its association with congenital cataract have not been documented.
source: The in-vivo function of PIKFYVE in the development of lens and its association with congenital cataract have not been documented.
evidence: Statement about the novelty of the findings.

claim: Previously reported PIKFYVE variants affecting the chaperonin-like domain cause fleck corneal dystrophy (CFD).
source: Different from previously reported PIKFYVE variants affecting the chaperonin-like domain that cause fleck corneal dystrophy (CFD), a disease characterized by tiny white flecks scattered in corneal stroma (Gee et al., 2015; Kawasaki et al., 2012; Li et al., 2005), the p.G1943E variant in the kinase domain of PIKFYVE was revealed for the first time to cause congenital cataract in human patients.
evidence: Supported by citations to Gee et al., 2015; Kawasaki et al., 2012; Li et al., 2005.

claim: Fleck corneal dystrophy (CFD) is characterized by tiny white flecks scattered in corneal stroma.
source: Different from previously reported PIKFYVE variants affecting the chaperonin-like domain that cause fleck corneal dystrophy (CFD), a disease characterized by tiny white flecks scattered in corneal stroma (Gee et al., 2015; Kawasaki et al., 2012; Li et al., 2005), the p.G1943E variant in the kinase domain of PIKFYVE was revealed for the first time to cause congenital cataract in human patients.
evidence: Supported by citations to Gee et al., 2015; Kawasaki et al., 2012; Li et al., 2005.

claim: The p.G1943E variant in the kinase domain of PIKFYVE was revealed for the first time to cause congenital cataract in human patients.
source: Different from previously reported PIKFYVE variants affecting the chaperonin-like domain that cause fleck corneal dystrophy (CFD), a disease characterized by tiny white flecks scattered in corneal stroma (Gee et al., 2015; Kawasaki et al., 2012; Li et al., 2005), the p.G1943E variant in the kinase domain of PIKFYVE was revealed for the first time to cause congenital cataract in human patients.
evidence: Based on the novelty of the finding in this study.

claim: Disruption of the PIPK domain in Pikfyve caused early-onset cataract defect in zebrafish.
source: Using zebrafish models, we demonstrated that disruption of the PIPK domain in Pikfyve caused early-onset cataract defect (aberrant accumulation of Rab7+Lc3+ amphisomes in the lens) and treating the pikfyve-deficient embryos with V-ATPase inhibitor bafilomycin A1 (Baf-A1) significantly alleviated the vacuolation defect in the lens of zebrafish mutants.
evidence: Zebrafish experiments showed early-onset cataract.

claim: The early-onset cataract defect in pikfyve zebrafish mutants is characterized by aberrant accumulation of Rab7+Lc3+ amphisomes in the lens.
source: Using zebrafish models, we demonstrated that disruption of the PIPK domain in Pikfyve caused early-onset cataract defect (aberrant accumulation of Rab7+Lc3+ amphisomes in the lens) and treating the pikfyve-deficient embryos with V-ATPase inhibitor bafilomycin A1 (Baf-A1) significantly alleviated the vacuolation defect in the lens of zebrafish mutants.
evidence: Marker analysis showed accumulation of Rab7+Lc3+ amphisomes.

claim: Treating pikfyve-deficient embryos with V-ATPase inhibitor bafilomycin A1 (Baf-A1) significantly alleviated the vacuolation defect in the lens of zebrafish mutants.
source: Using zebrafish models, we demonstrated that disruption of the PIPK domain in Pikfyve caused early-onset cataract defect (aberrant accumulation of Rab7+Lc3+ amphisomes in the lens) and treating the pikfyve-deficient embryos with V-ATPase inhibitor bafilomycin A1 (Baf-A1) significantly alleviated the vacuolation defect in the lens of zebrafish mutants.
evidence: Drug treatment experiments showed reduction in vacuolation.

claim: A large Chinese Korean family affected with congenital cataract consists of 31 family members including 12 affected individuals across four generations.
source: We recruited a large Chinese Korean family affected with congenital cataract, which consists of 31 family members including 12 affected individuals across four generations (Figure 1A).
evidence: Family pedigree analysis and Figure 1A show the family structure.

claim: Bilateral cataract was observed in every generation of the pedigree.
source: Bilateral cataract was observed in every generation of the pedigree and affected parents transmitted the disease to both males and females, suggesting an autosomal dominant inheritance.
evidence: Pedigree analysis showed bilateral cataract in all generations.

claim: Affected parents transmitted the disease to both males and females.
source: Bilateral cataract was observed in every generation of the pedigree and affected parents transmitted the disease to both males and females, suggesting an autosomal dominant inheritance.
evidence: Pedigree analysis showed transmission to both sexes.

claim: The inheritance pattern suggests an autosomal dominant inheritance.
source: Bilateral cataract was observed in every generation of the pedigree and affected parents transmitted the disease to both males and females, suggesting an autosomal dominant inheritance.
evidence: Inferred from the pedigree pattern.

claim: No other ocular and systemic abnormalities were found in the patients.
source: No other ocular and systemic abnormalities were found in these patients.
evidence: Clinical examination of patients.

claim: Seven of the 10 living patients were diagnosed as cataract in their first decade of life.
source: Clinical information was obtained from all patients except two deceased individuals (Table 1). Seven of the 10 living patients were diagnosed as cataract in their first decade of life, with the smallest age of diagnosis at 2 years old.
evidence: Clinical data from Table 1.

claim: The smallest age of diagnosis was at 2 years old.
source: Seven of the 10 living patients were diagnosed as cataract in their first decade of life, with the smallest age of diagnosis at 2 years old.
evidence: Clinical data from Table 1.

claim: The best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) of the patients ranged from 20/125 to 20/20.
source: The best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) of these patients ranged from 20/125 to 20/20.
evidence: Clinical data from Table 1.

claim: The proband (III-9) showed nuclear pulverulent cataract in both eyes.
source: The proband (III-9) showed nuclear pulverulent cataract in both eyes (Figure 1B) with vision loss (OD: 20/40, OS: 20/66) since childhood.
evidence: Clinical examination and Figure 1B show the cataract type.

claim: The proband (III-9) had vision loss (OD: 20/40, OS: 20/66) since childhood.
source: The proband (III-9) showed nuclear pulverulent cataract in both eyes (Figure 1B) with vision loss (OD: 20/40, OS: 20/66) since childhood.
evidence: Clinical data.

claim: The mother (II-4) of the proband had nuclear pulverulent cataract in both eyes.
source: The mother (II-4) of the proband also had nuclear pulverulent cataract in both eyes, while his father (II-3) had no cataract in either eye.
evidence: Clinical examination data.

claim: The father (II-3) of the proband had no cataract in either eye.
source: The mother (II-4) of the proband also had nuclear pulverulent cataract in both eyes, while his father (II-3) had no cataract in either eye.
evidence: Clinical examination data.

claim: The son (IV-5) of the proband had Y-sutural cataract.
source: The son (IV-5) of the proband had Y-sutural cataract.
evidence: Clinical examination data.

claim: Individuals II-8, III-5, III-6, and IV-3 presented nuclear pulverulent opacity in both eyes.
source: Among the other affected members of this family, individuals II-8, III-5, III-6, and IV-3 presented nuclear pulverulent opacity in both eyes, whereas individual III-1 and his son (IV-1) showed peripheral cortical punctate opacity in both eyes.
evidence: Clinical examination data.

claim: Individual III-1 and his son (IV-1) showed peripheral cortical punctate opacity in both eyes.
source: Among the other affected members of this family, individuals II-8, III-5, III-6, and IV-3 presented nuclear pulverulent opacity in both eyes, whereas individual III-1 and his son (IV-1) showed peripheral cortical punctate opacity in both eyes.
evidence: Clinical examination data.

claim: All patients of this family did not show any abnormities in fundus photography and optical coherence tomography (OCT) examinations.
source: All patients of this family did not show any abnormities in fundus photography and optical coherence tomography (OCT) examinations.
evidence: Clinical examination data.

claim: The PIKFYVE gene in the cataract patients carried a G to A heterozygous substitution in the 39th exon.
source: As shown in Figure 2A, in contrast to the healthy control, the PIKFYVE gene in the cataract patients carried a G to A heterozygous substitution in the 39th exon, which leads to the replacement of a highly conserved amino acid glycine (G) by glutamate (E) at position 1943 in the PIPK domain (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: Sanger sequencing results shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The G to A substitution in the 39th exon leads to the replacement of glycine (G) by glutamate (E) at position 1943 in the PIPK domain.
source: As shown in Figure 2A, in contrast to the healthy control, the PIKFYVE gene in the cataract patients carried a G to A heterozygous substitution in the 39th exon, which leads to the replacement of a highly conserved amino acid glycine (G) by glutamate (E) at position 1943 in the PIPK domain (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: Sequence analysis and protein alignment shown in Figure 2B and C.

claim: PIKFYVE is expressed in human anterior lens capsules.
source: To investigate the possible roles of PIKFYVE in the development of cataracts, we first confirmed its expression in human anterior lens capsules by quantitative RT-PCR (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: RT-PCR results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: The expression level of PIKFYVEG1943E was comparable with that of PIKFYVEWT.
source: As shown in Figure 2D, the expression level of PIKFYVEG1943E was comparable with that of PIKFYVEWT, suggesting that the p.G1943E variant has little or no effect on the protein stability of PIKFYVE.
evidence: Western blot analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The p.G1943E variant has little or no effect on the protein stability of PIKFYVE.
source: As shown in Figure 2D, the expression level of PIKFYVEG1943E was comparable with that of PIKFYVEWT, suggesting that the p.G1943E variant has little or no effect on the protein stability of PIKFYVE.
evidence: Inferred from comparable expression levels in Western blot.

claim: The p.G1943E sits in a linker connecting the N-lobe and the C-lobe of PIPK domain.
source: As shown in Figure 2E and F, the p.G1943E sits in a linker connecting the N-lobe (gold) and the C-lobe (cyan) of PIPK domain.
evidence: Structural modeling shown in Figure 2E and F.

claim: The loop acts as a hinge between N-lobe and C-lobe and forms a highly restricted conformation.
source: This loop (red) acts as a hinge between N-lobe and C-lobe (Figure 2F) and forms a highly restricted conformation.
evidence: Structural analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The p.G1943E variant introduces a negatively charged residue to the loop.
source: However, the p.G1943E variant introduces a negatively charged residue to the loop.
evidence: Based on the amino acid substitution from glycine to glutamate.

claim: The negatively charged residue changes the surface electrostatic potential of PIPK domain.
source: This negatively charged residue not only changes the surface electrostatic potential of PIPK domain (Figure 2G), but also generates charge repulsions between the loop and N-lobe (D1872 and D1871) (Figure 2F), thereby potentially affecting the kinase activity of PIKFYVE.
evidence: Electrostatic potential analysis shown in Figure 2G.

claim: The negatively charged residue generates charge repulsions between the loop and N-lobe (D1872 and D1871).
source: This negatively charged residue not only changes the surface electrostatic potential of PIPK domain (Figure 2G), but also generates charge repulsions between the loop and N-lobe (D1872 and D1871) (Figure 2F), thereby potentially affecting the kinase activity of PIKFYVE.
evidence: Structural analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The p.G1943E variant potentially affects the kinase activity of PIKFYVE.
source: This negatively charged residue not only changes the surface electrostatic potential of PIPK domain (Figure 2G), but also generates charge repulsions between the loop and N-lobe (D1872 and D1871) (Figure 2F), thereby potentially affecting the kinase activity of PIKFYVE.
evidence: Inferred from structural changes.

claim: Six affected loci from seven age-related or complicated cataract patients were identified.
source: To further strengthen the correlation of PIKFYVE variants with cataracts, we screened another congenital cataract family, 10 sporadic cases with congenital cataract and 200 patients with age-related or complicated cataract. In this experiment, six affected loci from seven age-related or complicated cataract patients were identified.
evidence: Screening results.

claim: Two variants in exon 36 (c.5399A>C, p.Q1800P) and exon 37 (c.5594C>T, p.A1865V) are located in the PIP kinase domain.
source: Among them, two variants in exon 36 (c.5399A>C, p.Q1800P) and exon 37 (c.5594C>T, p.A1865V) are located in the PIP kinase domain (Figure 2—figure supplement 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 2—source data 1).
evidence: Variant analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Genetic variants in PIKFYVE might be causal/risk factors for cataract formation.
source: These findings further suggested that genetic variants in PIKFYVE might be causal/risk factors for cataract formation.
evidence: Inferred from the identification of multiple variants in cataract patients.

claim: The pikfyveΔ8 allele harbored an 8 bp deletion and a 112 bp insertion in the cDNA of pikfyve.
source: To maximally mimic the p.G1943E variant in human patients, we designed single-guide RNA (sgRNA) in exon 40 to target the C terminal PIPK domain and screened out the pikfyveΔ8 allele, which harbored an 8 bp deletion and a 112 bp insertion in the cDNA of pikfyve.
evidence: Sequencing results of the mutant allele.

claim: The insertion/deletion in pikfyveΔ8 allele introduced a premature stop codon immediately downstream of the insertion site.
source: As shown in Figure 3A, this insertion/deletion in pikfyveΔ8 allele introduced a premature stop codon immediately downstream of the insertion site, thereby presumably generating a truncated Pikfyve protein that lacks the kinase activity.
evidence: Sequence analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The pikfyveΔ8 allele presumably generates a truncated Pikfyve protein that lacks the kinase activity.
source: As shown in Figure 3A, this insertion/deletion in pikfyveΔ8 allele introduced a premature stop codon immediately downstream of the insertion site, thereby presumably generating a truncated Pikfyve protein that lacks the kinase activity.
evidence: Inferred from the premature stop codon.

claim: pikfyveΔ8 homozygous mutants developed normally before 5 days post-fertilization (dpf).
source: Phenotypical analysis revealed that pikfyveΔ8 homozygous mutants developed normally before 5 days post-fertilization (dpf), but later showed severe developmental defects and all died by 9 dpf (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Phenotypical analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: pikfyveΔ8 homozygous mutants showed severe developmental defects after 5 dpf.
source: Phenotypical analysis revealed that pikfyveΔ8 homozygous mutants developed normally before 5 days post-fertilization (dpf), but later showed severe developmental defects and all died by 9 dpf (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Phenotypical analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: All pikfyveΔ8 homozygous mutants died by 9 dpf.
source: Phenotypical analysis revealed that pikfyveΔ8 homozygous mutants developed normally before 5 days post-fertilization (dpf), but later showed severe developmental defects and all died by 9 dpf (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Survival analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The lens of pikfyveΔ8 mutants was less transparent than siblings at 5 dpf.
source: Under stereomicroscope, we noticed that compared to siblings (sib), the lens of pikfyveΔ8 mutants was less transparent at 5 dpf (Figure 3B).
evidence: Microscopy observation shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Bubble-like vacuoles first appeared in the developing lens of pikfyveΔ8 homozygous mutants at 3 dpf.
source: Our results showed that bubble-like vacuoles first appeared in the developing lens of pikfyveΔ8 homozygous mutants at 3 dpf (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: DIC microscopy shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: The number and size of vacuoles both increased drastically by 5 dpf in pikfyveΔ8 homozygous mutants.
source: Strikingly, the number and size of vacuoles both increased drastically by 5 dpf and almost dominated the lens of mutants.
evidence: Microscopy observation and quantification.

claim: pikfyveΔ8 heterozygous mutants manifested significantly higher number of vacuoles in their lens compared to wild-type control.
source: Notably, compared to the wild-type (WT) control, pikfyveΔ8 heterozygous mutants also manifested significantly higher number of vacuoles in their lens (Figure 3C and D), suggesting that normal development of lens highly depends on the activity of Pikfyve and heterozygous disruption of Pikfyve is sufficient to cause cataract phenotype.
evidence: Microscopy and quantification shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: Normal development of lens highly depends on the activity of Pikfyve.
source: Notably, compared to the wild-type (WT) control, pikfyveΔ8 heterozygous mutants also manifested significantly higher number of vacuoles in their lens (Figure 3C and D), suggesting that normal development of lens highly depends on the activity of Pikfyve and heterozygous disruption of Pikfyve is sufficient to cause cataract phenotype.
evidence: Inferred from the phenotype of heterozygous mutants.

claim: Heterozygous disruption of Pikfyve is sufficient to cause cataract phenotype.
source: Notably, compared to the wild-type (WT) control, pikfyveΔ8 heterozygous mutants also manifested significantly higher number of vacuoles in their lens (Figure 3C and D), suggesting that normal development of lens highly depends on the activity of Pikfyve and heterozygous disruption of Pikfyve is sufficient to cause cataract phenotype.
evidence: Inferred from the phenotype of heterozygous mutants.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of PIKFYVE activity by inhibitor YM201636 induced aberrant vacuolation in human lens epithelial cells HLEB3.
source: Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of PIKFYVE activity by inhibitor YM201636 also induced aberrant vacuolation in human lens epithelial cells HLEB3 (Figure 3E and F), suggesting that the function of PIKFYVE in the regulation of cataract formation is highly conserved across species and our zebrafish cataract model would potentially be an excellent system for further preclinical study.
evidence: Cell culture experiments shown in Figure 3E and F.

claim: The function of PIKFYVE in the regulation of cataract formation is highly conserved across species.
source: Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of PIKFYVE activity by inhibitor YM201636 also induced aberrant vacuolation in human lens epithelial cells HLEB3 (Figure 3E and F), suggesting that the function of PIKFYVE in the regulation of cataract formation is highly conserved across species and our zebrafish cataract model would potentially be an excellent system for further preclinical study.
evidence: Inferred from similar phenotypes in human cells and zebrafish.

claim: The zebrafish cataract model would potentially be an excellent system for further preclinical study.
source: Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of PIKFYVE activity by inhibitor YM201636 also induced aberrant vacuolation in human lens epithelial cells HLEB3 (Figure 3E and F), suggesting that the function of PIKFYVE in the regulation of cataract formation is highly conserved across species and our zebrafish cataract model would potentially be an excellent system for further preclinical study.
evidence: Inferred from the conservation of function and phenotype.

claim: Both Tg(ubi:PIKFYVEWT) and Tg(ubi:PIKFYVEG1943E) zebrafish lines showed normal development of the lens during early stages.
source: As expected, both of these two zebrafish lines showed normal development of the lens during early stages (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B), suggesting that indeed haploinsufficiency, rather than dominant-negative inhibition of PIKFYVE activity by the p.G1943E variant caused cataract in human patients.
evidence: Microscopy observation shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The vacuolation phenotype could be partially rescued in both pikfyveΔ8;Tg(ubi:PIKFYVEWT) and pikfyveΔ8;Tg(ubi:PIKFYVEG1943E) zebrafish.
source: Moreover, the vacuolation phenotype could be partially rescued in both pikfyveΔ8;Tg(ubi:PIKFYVEWT) and pikfyveΔ8;Tg(ubi:PIKFYVEG1943E) zebrafish (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: Rescue experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A.

claim: The vacuole numbers decreased to less than 15 in all pikfyveΔ8;Tg(ubi:PIKFYVEWT) embryos.
source: However, while the vacuole numbers decreased to less than 15 in all pikfyveΔ8;Tg(ubi:PIKFYVEWT) embryos (n=6/6), about one-third of pikfyveΔ8;Tg(ubi:PIKFYVEG1943E) mutants still harbored more than 15 vacuoles (n=5/17) (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: Quantification shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A.

claim: About one-third of pikfyveΔ8;Tg(ubi:PIKFYVEG1943E) mutants still harbored more than 15 vacuoles.
source: However, while the vacuole numbers decreased to less than 15 in all pikfyveΔ8;Tg(ubi:PIKFYVEWT) embryos (n=6/6), about one-third of pikfyveΔ8;Tg(ubi:PIKFYVEG1943E) mutants still harbored more than 15 vacuoles (n=5/17) (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: Quantification shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A.

claim: The expression of PIKFYVE in Tg(ubi:PIKFYVEG1943E) was at least as strong as or even stronger than that of PIKFYVEWT.
source: As whole-mount in situ hybridization (WISH) results revealed that the expression of PIKFYVE in Tg(ubi:PIKFYVEG1943E) was at least as strong as or even stronger than that of PIKFYVEWT (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: WISH results shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The rescue effect of PIKFYVEG1943E is less efficient than that of PIKFYVEWT.
source: These results indicated that the rescue effect of PIKFYVEG1943E is less efficient than that of PIKFYVEWT.
evidence: Inferred from the differential rescue efficiency despite similar or higher expression.

claim: Vacuoles in pikfyveΔ8 mutants almost occupied the surface of the lens and all of them were DsRed negative.
source: Intriguingly, in comparison with evenly distributed DsRed signals in the lens of siblings, vacuoles in pikfyveΔ8 mutants almost occupied the surface of the lens and all of them were DsRed negative (Figure 4A), indicating that these vacuoles did not contain lens fibers.
evidence: Confocal imaging shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Vacuoles in pikfyveΔ8 mutants did not contain lens fibers.
source: Intriguingly, in comparison with evenly distributed DsRed signals in the lens of siblings, vacuoles in pikfyveΔ8 mutants almost occupied the surface of the lens and all of them were DsRed negative (Figure 4A), indicating that these vacuoles did not contain lens fibers.
evidence: Inferred from the absence of DsRed signal in vacuoles.

claim: Disruption of Pikfyve seemingly had no effects on the enucleation process of lens.
source: Meanwhile, hematoxylin-eosin (HE) staining, together with ZL-1 antibody and DAPI co-staining revealed that while disruption of Pikfyve seemingly had no effects on the enucleation process of lens, lens fibers in pikfyveΔ8 mutants were less organized than those in siblings (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: Histological analysis shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: Lens fibers in pikfyveΔ8 mutants were less organized than those in siblings.
source: Meanwhile, hematoxylin-eosin (HE) staining, together with ZL-1 antibody and DAPI co-staining revealed that while disruption of Pikfyve seemingly had no effects on the enucleation process of lens, lens fibers in pikfyveΔ8 mutants were less organized than those in siblings (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: Histological analysis shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: Large vacuoles were detected in the mutant lens at 3 dpf and 5 dpf.
source: We could detect large vacuoles in the mutant lens at 3 dpf and 5 dpf, while only several tiny vacuoles were observed in the sibling lens (Figure 4D).
evidence: TEM images shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Only several tiny vacuoles were observed in the sibling lens.
source: We could detect large vacuoles in the mutant lens at 3 dpf and 5 dpf, while only several tiny vacuoles were observed in the sibling lens (Figure 4D).
evidence: TEM images shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Lens fiber cells of siblings were mildly edema.
source: Lens fiber cells of siblings were mildly edema, and their nuclei were oval with uniform chromatin.
evidence: TEM analysis.

claim: The nuclei of lens fiber cells in siblings were oval with uniform chromatin.
source: Lens fiber cells of siblings were mildly edema, and their nuclei were oval with uniform chromatin.
evidence: TEM analysis.

claim: The lens fibers of siblings were arranged neatly and tightly.
source: The lens fibers (white arrows) were arranged neatly and tightly.
evidence: TEM analysis.

claim: Mitochondria of siblings were slightly swollen without vacuoles.
source: Furthermore, mitochondria (black triangles) of siblings were slightly swollen without vacuoles.
evidence: TEM analysis.

claim: Lens fiber cells of the pikfyveΔ8 mutants were obviously edematous.
source: In contrast, lens fiber cells of the pikfyveΔ8 mutants were obviously edematous and the nuclei were irregularly shaped.
evidence: TEM analysis.

claim: The nuclei of lens fiber cells in pikfyveΔ8 mutants were irregularly shaped.
source: In contrast, lens fiber cells of the pikfyveΔ8 mutants were obviously edematous and the nuclei were irregularly shaped.
evidence: TEM analysis.

claim: The arrangement of lens fibers in pikfyveΔ8 mutants was loose and deformed.
source: Besides, the arrangement of lens fibers was loose and deformed and lipid droplets were formed in pikfyveΔ8 mutants.
evidence: TEM analysis.

claim: Lipid droplets were formed in pikfyveΔ8 mutants.
source: Besides, the arrangement of lens fibers was loose and deformed and lipid droplets were formed in pikfyveΔ8 mutants.
evidence: TEM analysis.

claim: Mitochondria of pikfyveΔ8 mutants were obviously swollen and enlarged compared to siblings.
source: Compared to the siblings, mitochondria (black triangles) of pikfyveΔ8 mutants were obviously swollen and enlarged.
evidence: TEM analysis.

claim: Mitochondrial crests were reduced in pikfyveΔ8 mutants.
source: Mitochondrial crests were reduced, and most of them were aberrantly vacuolated.
evidence: TEM analysis.

claim: Most mitochondria in pikfyveΔ8 mutants were aberrantly vacuolated.
source: Mitochondrial crests were reduced, and most of them were aberrantly vacuolated.
evidence: TEM analysis.

claim: Autophagic lysosomes appeared swollen and vacuolated in pikfyveΔ8 mutants.
source: In addition, autophagic lysosomes also appeared swollen and vacuolated in pikfyveΔ8 mutants.
evidence: TEM analysis.

claim: Vacuoles in pikfyveΔ8 mutants were highly dynamic.
source: Our results showed that vacuoles in pikfyveΔ8 mutants were highly dynamic and small vacuoles were frequently found to be fused with each other to form larger ones (Figure 5A, white arrows).
evidence: Time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Small vacuoles in pikfyveΔ8 mutants were frequently found to be fused with each other to form larger ones.
source: Our results showed that vacuoles in pikfyveΔ8 mutants were highly dynamic and small vacuoles were frequently found to be fused with each other to form larger ones (Figure 5A, white arrows).
evidence: Time-lapse imaging shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Almost all vacuoles in pikfyveΔ8 mutants were positive for the late endosome maker Rab7-GFP.
source: Our results showed that in pikfyveΔ8 mutants, almost all vacuoles were positive for the late endosome maker Rab7-GFP (Figure 5C, white arrows).
evidence: Marker analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The early endosome marker Rab5c-GFP showed no co-localization with vacuoles in pikfyveΔ8 mutants.
source: By contrast, the early endosome marker Rab5c-GFP and recycling marker Rab11a-GFP showed no co-localization with vacuoles (Figure 5B-D).
evidence: Marker analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The recycling marker Rab11a-GFP showed no co-localization with vacuoles in pikfyveΔ8 mutants.
source: By contrast, the early endosome marker Rab5c-GFP and recycling marker Rab11a-GFP showed no co-localization with vacuoles (Figure 5B-D).
evidence: Marker analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: A proportion of vacuoles in pikfyveΔ8 mutants were positive for the autophagosome marker Lc3b.
source: As shown in Figure 5 and a proportion of vacuoles in pikfyveΔ8 mutants were also positive for the autophagosome marker Lc3b.
evidence: Marker analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Vacuoles in pikfyveΔ8 mutants were amphisomes formed by the fusion of autophagosomes and late endosomes.
source: Taken together, these data implied that vacuoles in pikfyveΔ8 mutants were amphisomes formed by the fusion of autophagosomes and late endosomes.
evidence: Inferred from co-localization with Rab7 and Lc3b markers.

claim: The vacuole phenotype induced by PIKFYVE deficiency in COS-7 cells could be rescued by Baf-A1.
source: Baf-A1 is a specific inhibitor of V-ATPase. Previous work has shown that the vacuole phenotype induced by PIKFYVE deficiency in COS-7 cells could be rescued by Baf-A1 (Compton et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Compton et al., 2016.

claim: Vacuole number in the lens of Baf-A1-treated pikfyveΔ8 mutants was significantly lower than that in the control group treated with DMSO.
source: Indeed, we found that vacuole number in the lens of Baf-A1-treated pikfyveΔ8 mutants was significantly lower than that in the control group treated with dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: Drug treatment experiments shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: Vacuole numbers of all the mutant embryos showed a slight increase after DMSO treatment or without treatment.
source: As shown in Figure 6C and D, while vacuole numbers of all the mutant embryos showed a slight increase after DMSO treatment or without treatment, we observed significant decrease of vacuole numbers in all pikfyveΔ8 mutants.
evidence: Time-course imaging shown in Figure 6C and D.

claim: Significant decrease of vacuole numbers was observed in all pikfyveΔ8 mutants after Baf-A1 treatment.
source: As shown in Figure 6C and D, while vacuole numbers of all the mutant embryos showed a slight increase after DMSO treatment or without treatment, we observed significant decrease of vacuole numbers in all pikfyveΔ8 mutants.
evidence: Time-course imaging shown in Figure 6C and D.

claim: Overexpression of TRPML1 partially rescued the vacuole phenotype in PIKFYVE-deficient macrophages.
source: On the other hand, a previous study also showed overexpression of transient receptor potential mucolipin 1 (TRPML1) could partially rescue the vacuole phenotype in PIKfyve-deficient macrophages (Krishna et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Krishna et al., 2016.

claim: Ectopic expression of Trpml1 by mRNA injection failed to rescue vacuolation phenotype in pikfyveΔ8 mutants.
source: However, in our system, ectopic expression of Trpml1 by mRNA injection failed to rescue vacuolation phenotype in pikfyveΔ8 mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Rescue experiments shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: V-ATPase rather than Trpml1 might be a key component for the formation or maintenance of the large vacuoles in the lens of pikfyve-deficient mutants.
source: Thus, V-ATPase rather than Trpml1 might be a key component for the formation or maintenance of the large vacuoles in the lens of pikfyve-deficient mutants, and inhibition of V-ATPase by Baf-A1 could directly alleviate the cataract phenotype.
evidence: Inferred from the differential rescue effects of Baf-A1 and Trpml1.

claim: Inhibition of V-ATPase by Baf-A1 could directly alleviate the cataract phenotype.
source: Thus, V-ATPase rather than Trpml1 might be a key component for the formation or maintenance of the large vacuoles in the lens of pikfyve-deficient mutants, and inhibition of V-ATPase by Baf-A1 could directly alleviate the cataract phenotype.
evidence: Based on the rescue effect of Baf-A1.

claim: The p.G1943E variant is very rare in the general population.
source: In this study, we identified a missense variant (p.G1943E) in PIKFYVE responsible for congenital cataract in a Chinese Korean family (Figures 1 and 2). This variant is very rare in the general population.
evidence: Based on gnomAD database frequency.

claim: In the gnomAD database, only four individuals carry the p.G1943E variant.
source: In the gnomAD database, only four individuals (including three East Asians and one Latino/Admixed American) carry the p.G1943E variant, representing an extremely low allele frequency of 0.00002 (Table 2).
evidence: Data from gnomAD database shown in Table 2.

claim: The p.G1943E variant has an extremely low allele frequency of 0.00002.
source: In the gnomAD database, only four individuals (including three East Asians and one Latino/Admixed American) carry the p.G1943E variant, representing an extremely low allele frequency of 0.00002 (Table 2).
evidence: Data from gnomAD database shown in Table 2.

claim: The degree and morphology of lens opacity in the cataract family were phenotypically heterogeneous.
source: Consistent with previous findings (Berry et al., 2020b), the degree and morphology of lens opacity in the cataract family were phenotypically heterogeneous (Table 1).
evidence: Clinical data from Table 1 and citation to Berry et al., 2020b.

claim: Most of the patients in this family developed cataract and vision loss in their childhood.
source: While most of the patients in this family developed cataract and vision loss in their childhood, some cases were diagnosed quite late.
evidence: Clinical data from Table 1.

claim: Some cases in the family were diagnosed quite late.
source: While most of the patients in this family developed cataract and vision loss in their childhood, some cases were diagnosed quite late.
evidence: Clinical data from Table 1.

claim: The majority of patients had nuclear pulverulent cataract.
source: Meanwhile, the majority of patients had nuclear pulverulent cataract, while the others had nuclear Y-sutural cataract or peripheral cortical punctate cataract (Table 1).
evidence: Clinical data from Table 1.

claim: Some patients had nuclear Y-sutural cataract or peripheral cortical punctate cataract.
source: Meanwhile, the majority of patients had nuclear pulverulent cataract, while the others had nuclear Y-sutural cataract or peripheral cortical punctate cataract (Table 1).
evidence: Clinical data from Table 1.

claim: The heterogeneity in clinical manifestations might be ascribed to interactions between genetic and environmental factors during lens development.
source: This heterogeneity in clinical manifestations might be ascribed to interactions between genetic and environmental factors during lens development (Berry et al., 2020b).
evidence: Supported by citation to Berry et al., 2020b.

claim: Variants in PIKFYVE have been reported to be associated with CFD.
source: Variants in PIKFYVE have been reported to be associated with CFD (Gee et al., 2015; Kawasaki et al., 2012; Kotoulas et al., 2011; Li et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citations to Gee et al., 2015; Kawasaki et al., 2012; Kotoulas et al., 2011; Li et al., 2005.

claim: Two of the CFD patients showed cataract formation at 66 and 58 years old, respectively.
source: However, except that two of the CFD patients showed cataract formation at 66 and 58 years old, respectively, none of these PIKFYVE variants in these studies caused congenital cataract (Kotoulas et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kotoulas et al., 2011.

claim: None of the PIKFYVE variants associated with CFD caused congenital cataract except for two late-onset cases.
source: However, except that two of the CFD patients showed cataract formation at 66 and 58 years old, respectively, none of these PIKFYVE variants in these studies caused congenital cataract (Kotoulas et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kotoulas et al., 2011.

claim: No corneal defect was observed in patients with congenital cataract in this study.
source: Interestingly, we also did not observe any corneal defect in patients with congenital cataract in this study.
evidence: Clinical examination.

claim: All CFD-related mutations in PIKFYVE are distributed in two regions (amino acids 667–843 and 1490–1538).
source: It is noted that all CFD-related mutations in PIKFYVE, either homozygous or heterozygous, are distributed in two regions (i.e., amino acids 667–843 and 1490–1538), corresponding to cytosolic chaperone CCTγ apical domain-like motif and SPEC domains, respectively.
evidence: Analysis of reported mutations.

claim: The two regions of CFD-related mutations correspond to cytosolic chaperone CCTγ apical domain-like motif and SPEC domains.
source: It is noted that all CFD-related mutations in PIKFYVE, either homozygous or heterozygous, are distributed in two regions (i.e., amino acids 667–843 and 1490–1538), corresponding to cytosolic chaperone CCTγ apical domain-like motif and SPEC domains, respectively.
evidence: Analysis of reported mutations and protein domains.

claim: Different domains of PIKFYVE might exert different functions by binding with different partners.
source: Based on these findings, we hypothesized that different domains of PIKFYVE might exert different functions by binding with different partners.
evidence: Hypothesis based on the differential disease phenotypes associated with different domains.

claim: The p.G1943E variant only mildly altered the 3-D conformation of PIPK domain by changing its surface electrostatic potential and generating charge repulsions between the loop and N-lobe.
source: First, the predicted protein structure suggested that, instead of gross disruption of PIKFYVE protein structure, the p.G1943E variant only mildly altered the 3-D conformation of PIPK domain by changing its surface electrostatic potential and generating charge repulsions between the loop and N-lobe (Figure 2G and F).
evidence: Structural modeling shown in Figure 2G and F.

claim: The p.G1943E mutation in PIPK domain may specifically alter its kinase activity or change the binding surface with other proteins.
source: Therefore, it is reasonable to argue that this mutation in PIPK domain may specifically alter its kinase activity or change the binding surface with other proteins, while keep the N-terminal cytosolic chaperone CCTγ apical domain-like motif and SPEC domains functional intact.
evidence: Inferred from structural analysis.

claim: The p.G1943E mutation keeps the N-terminal cytosolic chaperone CCTγ apical domain-like motif and SPEC domains functionally intact.
source: Therefore, it is reasonable to argue that this mutation in PIPK domain may specifically alter its kinase activity or change the binding surface with other proteins, while keep the N-terminal cytosolic chaperone CCTγ apical domain-like motif and SPEC domains functional intact.
evidence: Inferred from the location of the mutation.

claim: The C-terminal PIPK domain was truncated in PikfyveΔ8 protein.
source: Second, in our pikfyveΔ8 zebrafish mutants, while the C-terminal PIPK domain was truncated in PikfyveΔ8 protein, the N-terminal cytosolic chaperone CCTγ apical domain-like motif and SPEC domains were not affected.
evidence: Based on the mutation design and sequence analysis.

claim: The N-terminal cytosolic chaperone CCTγ apical domain-like motif and SPEC domains were not affected in pikfyveΔ8 mutants.
source: Second, in our pikfyveΔ8 zebrafish mutants, while the C-terminal PIPK domain was truncated in PikfyveΔ8 protein, the N-terminal cytosolic chaperone CCTγ apical domain-like motif and SPEC domains were not affected.
evidence: Based on the mutation design and sequence analysis.

claim: No cornea defect was observed in the zebrafish mutants.
source: Accordingly, we did not observe any cornea defect in the zebrafish mutants either.
evidence: Phenotypical analysis of zebrafish mutants.

claim: Inhibition of PIKFYVE in COS-7 cells induced large vacuoles through promoting the enlargement of both early and late endosomes.
source: Inhibition of PIKFYVE in COS-7 cells had been shown to induce large vacuoles through promoting the enlargement of both early and late endosomes (Ikonomov et al., 2006; Rutherford et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to Ikonomov et al., 2006; Rutherford et al., 2006.

claim: The Ca2+ releasing channel endolysosome-localized mucolipin TRPML1 acts downstream of PIKFYVE to trigger membrane fusion/fission process.
source: Further studies revealed that the Ca2+ releasing channel endolysosome-localized mucolipin TRPML1 acts downstream of PIKFYVE to trigger membrane fusion/fission process (Dong et al., 2010) or promote lysosome/phagosome maturation (Dayam et al., 2015; Kim et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Dong et al., 2010; Dayam et al., 2015; Kim et al., 2014.

claim: TRPML1 acts downstream of PIKFYVE to promote lysosome/phagosome maturation.
source: Further studies revealed that the Ca2+ releasing channel endolysosome-localized mucolipin TRPML1 acts downstream of PIKFYVE to trigger membrane fusion/fission process (Dong et al., 2010) or promote lysosome/phagosome maturation (Dayam et al., 2015; Kim et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Dong et al., 2010; Dayam et al., 2015; Kim et al., 2014.

claim: PIKFYVE might function in a context-dependent manner.
source: Interestingly, while overexpression of TRPML1 partially alleviated the vacuole phenotype in PIKFYVE-deficient macrophages (Krishna et al., 2016), the rescue effect was not observed in the lens of pikfyveΔ8 zebrafish mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), suggesting that PIKFYVE might function in a context-dependent manner.
evidence: Inferred from differential rescue effects in different cell types.

claim: Vacuoles in microglia and lens cells of pikfyveΔ8 mutants were differently stained by lysosome marker.
source: Consistent with this idea, we also noted that vacuoles in microglia (the brain-resident macrophages) and lens cells of pikfyveΔ8 mutants were differently stained by lysosome marker (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Marker staining shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Vacuole formation in PIKFYVE-deficient COS-7 cells and macrophages could be inhibited by Baf-A1.
source: On the other hand, vacuole formation in PIKFYVE-deficient COS-7 cells and macrophages could also be inhibited by a drug called Baf-A1 (Compton et al., 2016; Isobe et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Compton et al., 2016; Isobe et al., 2019.

claim: Baf-A1 is a macrolide antibiotic that inhibits V-ATPase.
source: Baf-A1 is a macrolide antibiotic that inhibits V-ATPase, the ATP-dependent proton pump located on the membrane of organelles.
evidence: General knowledge about Baf-A1.

claim: V-ATPase is the ATP-dependent proton pump located on the membrane of organelles.
source: Baf-A1 is a macrolide antibiotic that inhibits V-ATPase, the ATP-dependent proton pump located on the membrane of organelles.
evidence: General knowledge about V-ATPase.

claim: The cellular acidification process mediated by V-ATPase may affect membrane trafficking.
source: The cellular acidification process mediated by V-ATPase may affect many basic biological processes, including membrane trafficking (in particular endosome maturation and fusion between autophagosomes and lysosomes; Hammond et al., 1998; Yamamoto et al., 1998), protein degradation, and autophagy (Bowman et al., 1988; Yamamoto et al., 1998; Yoshimori et al., 1991).
evidence: Supported by citations to Hammond et al., 1998; Yamamoto et al., 1998.

claim: The cellular acidification process mediated by V-ATPase may affect protein degradation.
source: The cellular acidification process mediated by V-ATPase may affect many basic biological processes, including membrane trafficking (in particular endosome maturation and fusion between autophagosomes and lysosomes; Hammond et al., 1998; Yamamoto et al., 1998), protein degradation, and autophagy (Bowman et al., 1988; Yamamoto et al., 1998; Yoshimori et al., 1991).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bowman et al., 1988; Yamamoto et al., 1998; Yoshimori et al., 1991.

claim: The cellular acidification process mediated by V-ATPase may affect autophagy.
source: The cellular acidification process mediated by V-ATPase may affect many basic biological processes, including membrane trafficking (in particular endosome maturation and fusion between autophagosomes and lysosomes; Hammond et al., 1998; Yamamoto et al., 1998), protein degradation, and autophagy (Bowman et al., 1988; Yamamoto et al., 1998; Yoshimori et al., 1991).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bowman et al., 1988; Yamamoto et al., 1998; Yoshimori et al., 1991.

claim: Mutations in V-ATPase in yeast that did not affect proton pump function caused defects in vacuole fusion.
source: Interestingly, several works in yeast also identified mutations in V-ATPase that did not affect proton pump function, but indeed caused defects in vacuole fusion (Strasser et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Strasser et al., 2011.

claim: Inhibition of vesicle fusion by Baf-A1 in Drosophila did not depend on V-ATPases, but relied on Ca2+ SERCA pump.
source: Moreover, another study in Drosophila demonstrated that inhibition of vesicle fusion by Baf-A1 did not depend on V-ATPases, but relied on Ca2+ sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase (SERCA) pump, the secondary target of Baf-A1 (Mauvezin et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Mauvezin et al., 2015.
